IA-2025-HCR105.policyArea: major economic growth attraction program, resolutions, resolutions-policy
IA-2025-HCR105.aiSummary: The resolution would set the agenda for the first extraordinary session of the 2026 Iowa legislative session. It would limit that session to a bill on the major economic growth attraction program, including its effective date, and to any other resolutions either chamber adopts.

IA-2025-SF473.aiSummary: The law changes child foster care and adoption rules for some people and groups with sincere religious or moral beliefs about sexual orientation or gender identity. It says the state cannot require certain foster caregivers or adoptive parents to agree with beliefs that conflict with their own, and it lets them sue or ask the attorney general to enforce the rule. It also says religious groups that work with the state on foster care or adoption cannot be forced to provide those services in a way that conflicts with their beliefs, while the state still must look at a child’s best interests.

IA-2025-SF2453.policyArea: business assistance, colleges and universities, innovation
IA-2025-SF2453.aiSummary: The bill would have required Iowa’s public universities to invest at least 1% of their endowment assets in certified innovation funds by July 1, 2027. It would have let the regents grant a one-year waiver and could have cut some state funding if an institution did not comply. The bill would also have required yearly reports and a public list of eligible funds, and it was vetoed by the governor.

IA-2025-HF2254.aiSummary: The law bars the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics from putting noncompete clauses in job contracts with certain health workers, including nurses, pharmacists, physicians, and physician assistants. IA-2025-HF2230.title: A bill for an act relating to teacher education and licensing, including by modifying provisions related to practitioner preparation programs and licenses issued by the board of educational examiners.

Read first time, attached to SF 2222.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.

IA-2025-HF2230.policyArea: education, educational examiners board, english learners
IA-2025-HF2230.aiSummary: Signed into law, this measure changes teacher training and licensing in Iowa. Starting July 1, 2027, teacher prep programs must include more training and practice on teaching students with disabilities and English learners, and students must pass a final end-of-program test for their license area. It also requires people seeking a special education teaching job to complete a state-made self-paced course on special education laws, testing, and key skills before getting a class B or conditional license.

IA-2025-SF2189.title: A bill for an act relating to information required for nonresidents who apply for vehicle registration and issuance of a certificate of title.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by President and Speaker, and sent to Governor.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.
Read first time, referred to Transportation.

IA-2025-SF2189.policyArea: certificates of title, driver's licenses, motor vehicle registration
IA-2025-SF2189.aiSummary: This law changes the information nonresidents must give when they apply to register a vehicle or get an Iowa title. It requires the application to include the primary user’s name, Iowa driver’s license or nonoperator ID number, birth date, residence, and mailing address, or the business’s address and federal tax ID if the user is a business. For a nonresident who owns Iowa property and mainly uses the vehicle there, the application may use proof of property ownership and may use an out-of-state driver’s license or ID number instead of some of the Iowa information. The state agency must set rules for what counts as proof of property ownership.

IA-2025-SF2426.aiSummary: The law adds English-language checks for people who apply for or renew a commercial driver’s license or commercial learner’s permit in Iowa. Drivers who cannot show enough English skill may be denied a license or permit, and people who do not meet the rule may not operate a commercial vehicle; the law also sets penalties for drivers and motor carriers that violate it. The new license check starts on March 1, 2027, or when the transportation department says its new records system is ready, whichever comes first.

IA-2025-SF2480.aiSummary: The law changes Iowa rules for alternative nicotine products and vapor products, which are nicotine items that are not tobacco. It adds new taxes on these products, set at 5 cents per container for alternative nicotine products and 5 cents per milliliter for vapor products, and it updates who is treated as a distributor, manufacturer, or seller for tax purposes. It also sets aside the first $3 million each year from these new taxes, starting July 1, 2027, for pediatric cancer research and related care at the University of Iowa Stead Family Children's Hospital.

IA-2025-SF2231.aiSummary: Iowa enacted a law that changes school rules on student speech and religious expression, and it requires the education department to share federal guidance and model policies with schools. It also changes preschool program rules for four-year-old children and sets new rules for some charter schools and innovation zone schools to follow the same protected speech standards as school districts. The law also updates some college credit and shared-time education program rules for high school students.

IA-2025-HF571.title: A bill for an act relating to protections for medical practitioners and health care institutions, including those related to the exercise of conscience, whistleblower activities, and free speech, and providing penalties.

Read first time, attached to SF 220.

IA-2025-HF571.policyArea: freedom of speech, health-related professions, medical care
IA-2025-HF571.aiSummary: Becomes law in Iowa as the Medical Ethics Defense Act. It protects medical practitioners and health care institutions from certain penalties or discrimination when they refuse to take part in care for conscience reasons, report possible violations, or engage in speech or other protected expression. It also sets rules for complaints and can fine a licensing or certifying agency $500 per day if it does not share a complaint within 21 days.

IA-2025-HF2788.title: A bill for an act relating to abortions including definitions, informed consent, dispensing of abortion-inducing drugs, and other abortion-related provisions.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, referred to Appropriations.
Amendment H-8433 to amendment H-8432 adopted.

IA-2025-HF2788.aiSummary: Iowa's new law changes how abortion is defined and adds new rules for informed consent. It requires an in-person exam before an abortion, adds steps and warnings before abortion drugs are prescribed or given, and limits where those drugs can be dispensed. It also creates civil liability and license discipline for people who violate the drug rules, and it changes what must be reported about abortions and miscarriages.

IA-2025-HF2515.aiSummary: The law changes Iowa rules on deferred or suspended sentences, which are sentence options that delay or lessen punishment. It adds cases under section 728.12, which covers sexual exploitation of a minor, to the list of offenses affected. It became law as Chapter 1023.
